Since \(f(x)\ge 0\) for all \(x\), we must have \(a>0\) and discriminant \(\le 0\), so
\[
b^2-4ac\le 0 \implies c\ge \frac{b^2}{4a}.
\]
The denominator \(b-a>0\), so for fixed \(a,b\), minimize by taking
\[
c=\frac{b^2}{4a}.
\]
Let \(b=ta\) with \(t>1\). Then
\[
\frac{a+b+c}{b-a}
=
\frac{a+ta+\frac{t^2a}{4}}{ta-a}
=
\frac{1+t+\frac{t^2}{4}}{t-1}
=
\frac{(t+2)^2}{4(t-1)}.
\]
Minimize
\[
g(t)=\frac{(t+2)^2}{4(t-1)},\quad t>1.
\]
\[
g'(t)=\frac{(t+2)(t-4)}{4(t-1)^2}.
\]
Thus \(g\) is minimized at \(t=4\), giving
\[
g(4)=\frac{6^2}{4\cdot 3}=3.
\]
\[
\boxed{3}
\]
